note: Arkema beat its own compiled EBITDA consensus in Q1 (+6%) and Q2 (+8%) and the Q3 bar of EUR328m implies a slowdown on an easy comp while every chemicals peer reported strong price pass-through; beats have been bought on each of the last four results days, but the FY guide risk on Q4 Middle East commentary cuts against and this is a 17-analyst mega-cap, so the lean is modest.

A FIRST FY2026/27 guide on a name whose last two guidance events moved -15.8% and -15.75% sets abs_move high; the hunter's sourced correction of the baseline (6.08% disclosed net short on the DFSA register, 4th largest in Denmark, barely covered through a 32% rally, recorded as 0.0 by a name-join defect) is real squeeze fuel, and the unbooked DKK 155m tariff tranche leans up, but the direction of a first guide after two growth cuts is close to balanced.

The Q3 margin was pre-released at ~3% on the 5 Oct pre-close call so the quarter is worth 0; what is left is the guide decision, and reaching the low end of 3.0-4.0% needs a Q4 margin of 5.2-5.4% off a 9M near 2.2%, with management refusing to commit on the call and Jefferies flagging recoveries slipping to 2027 — prints with an unchanged guide have been sold on this name.

FY26 is pre-released, so the move lives in the first FY27 guide and in the first statement on whether the 6 Oct cyber incident hit demand; the stock sits at 428p against 502p pre-incident and below its pre-upgrade level although the FY26 upgrade stands, on an observed reaction history whose last three events were 11-14%. Held to a modest p_up because ASOS finals with a new-year guide fell -6.5% and -5.3% and the post-update FY27 bar is unsourced.

The FY26 ~USD700m guide implies only ~USD171m a quarter against a Q2 of 192.1m and a rising backlog, so a raise or firmer guide is the likely guidance event on a name whose observed results-day median is 13.5%; but no Q3 consensus could be sourced, seven brokers already raised targets after Q2 and KION's flat Dematic orders cut against, so the certainty stays near 50 while the size stays large.

Near-nothing: the NRE I carry, the fee step-up and the October refinancing are all explicitly in the two public previews, the company gives only a qualitative outlook, and the only open lines are Q3 fair-value changes and fundraising commentary, where Inderes has already written the NRE IV risk into its note.

Two sides that nearly cancel: Volvo CE orders +16% and Caterpillar Construction +18% against an easy Q3 2025 order comp, with the stock falling after both prints and insiders buying, versus a near-certain revenue-guide narrowing (FY consensus implies Q4 +33%) and an FCF guide that needs +EUR100m in H2 after H1 at -29.7m. The negatives agree with a 4.31% short that is building, so they are the half more likely already in the price.

The release carries DIS's own Q4-to-date fixtures against peer books of USD56-60k for MR and USD106k for LR1 while Equita's H2 assumption is ~USD30k, plus the interim-dividend slot that moved the stock +7.5% on the 2025 equivalent; sized down hard because the hunter's own finding 3 shows the sector selling exactly this news (TORM beat, raised and paid USD1.35 and fell 6.2%) and DIS's ~55% time-charter cover at ~USD24k caps the blended uplift.

A real guidance event the company itself scheduled for November (the cost guide, with AI efficiencies) plus a probable EUR250-300m buyback and JPM's above-consensus EBITDA, into a 4.5% give-back from the record on the CEO news; but this is a 14-analyst name whose consensus was compiled after the volume tables, so only the SIZE of the cut is unpriced and the whole set sits in the wire copy.

Fineco pre-releases net sales, deposits and brokerage every month, so the quarter is worth 0; the only open line is how much of the September ECB hike management folds into the 2026 outlook, and outlook tweaks moved this stock +4.65% and +1.28% before. Low-vol, 27-analyst name and a 4.6% market-wide gain already taken on 4 Nov.

Both the quarter and the guide went out in the 24 Sep ad-hoc, so the print carries only Q4/2027 shape and 9M cash flow; the cut FY guide needs Q4 AEBITDA roughly flat year on year on revenue down ~10% and the one sourced broker estimate already sits at the bottom, while the stock has rallied 19% in 20 days to above its pre-warning level with no operational trigger. A 7.8% short that is covering rather than building is the main thing holding p_up near 50.

The 21 Oct target raise (made after Q3 closed) implies H2 sales of SEK1,301-1,401m against the only published bar, ABG's stale Q3 580m which has not been updated since 14 Oct; the last three reports beat that same bar and moved +9.7%, +6.8% and +9.4%, and at $216k a day of turnover nobody is positioned. Discounted for the revenue being effectively pre-released by the guide and for the working-capital risk on cash flow.

Legrand's published bar was collected 5-9 Oct, before Schneider (+16.9% organic, guide raised), Vertiv (orders +100%), nVent (+44%), Eaton (Electrical Americas +22%) and, decisively, its largest distributor Rexel (+11.4% against a 6.6% consensus, Europe +4.5% against Legrand's implied -0.6%); the stock de-rated 11% with the AI-capex trade instead. Capped because this name's own history is that misses are punished (-12.2%) and beats are ignored (-1.7%, -0.35%) and the whisper has probably moved above the 9 Oct sheet.

A guidance day squared: the FY26 ~NOK7.5bn guide needs H2 revenue up ~30% after an H1 down 6%, and the same 07:00 release carries a Capital Markets Update whose 2028 targets (>NOK10bn, >5% EBIT) stand against 2027 consensus of NOK7.02bn, with Q3 announced order flow of only ~NOK0.45bn against ~NOK1.9bn of quarterly revenue. The last two prints that leaned on the H2 ramp fell 5.1% and 13.7%; consensus already below the guide and insider buying are what keep this from being larger.

The 8 Oct pre-close call pre-released everything that matters — normal wind speeds, the Revolution Wind and Changhua ramp, 'Offshore higher' and the ~DKK3.5bn non-cash impairment — so the quarter and the write-down are worth 0; Vattenfall's Wind EBITDA +64% on flat volumes argues mildly for a firmer guide, against a +8.5% five-day entry close driven by the US midterms that raises the bar for the US section.

The two real items offset on a 20-broker consensus: the NII bar of 6,357 is only ~+1.7% underlying once the Q2 CJEU -173m is added back, against peers in line to +3.6%, while the impairment line is consensus-down 3.7% q/q even though mBank came 30% and Pekao 7% above their bars on corporate provisions. P2G at zero and the CEO's 'strongest year' ambition add a little; the CHF line was pre-released at exactly the consensus and is worth 0.

Customer-level volume evidence is strong — Wabash shipped 9,563 trailers against 6,675 and ACT put September US net trailer orders 311% above the year before, against SAF Americas at -1.3% organic in H1 and a weak Q3 2025 base — while the stock fell 6.7% since 21 Oct. The same Wabash document is the counterweight: it missed its own guide, burned cash, guided Q4 down and described rival discounting, which is margin pressure suppliers absorb.

A mechanical, dated negative: Skanska blamed Q2's SEK-464m US Commercial Property write-down on a 14bp rise in the US 10-year, and in Q3 that yield rose 85bp to 5.29% on 30 September, the appraisal date, with only SEK822m of unrealised gain on SEK18.5bn of completed book — and the prior-quarter consensus carries no impairment, as in Q3 2025 when PBT missed by 21% and the stock fell 4.7%. The price has gone the other way to a 2026 high as the yield eased after the appraisal; the strong NCC, Peab and JM prints are a genuine Nordic offset and the name is low-vol, which caps the size.

The guidance event was taken out of this print by the 27 Oct ad-hoc, and the line that drove the name's worst print (Q3 2025 orders, -21%) has been pre-signalled positive — 'high level' intake, a record order book above EUR473.7m, Berenberg expecting higher Q3 orders, Besi orders +17% q/q — with the figure itself unpublished and the stock down 23% in 20 days and 39% in 60. Held back because the sector sold Besi's good order print and Q2's record orders barely moved this stock, and the Q3 margin and working capital will be ugly.

The best unpriced mechanism on the sheet: Italian PSV gas averaged 75.4 EUR/MWh in September 2026 against ~35 a year earlier and 58.3 in August, where Q2 was mild, on a two-analyst name that discloses neither its hedge ratio nor its pass-through — and the last comparable energy shock (Q1 2025) took the EBITDA margin from 21.8% to 14.2% and the stock -10.33% on the day. O-I independently says European energy and freight ran ~$15m above plan and its Europe segment profit fell from $95m to $2m, while the stock is up 6.7% in 20 days into the print with one unchanged 0.5% short. Offset by Zignago's own easy Q3 2025 base and Verallia saying Italy held steady.
